transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because things have been feeling a little hard to explain, and I don’t want to sound dramatic. For months now, I’ve been trying to get people to see that my husband’s family is, um… quietly interfering with our money and our reputation.

Like, little billing errors will show up at work, or someone at church will suddenly act strange toward me, and it just feels connected. People will pull up records and say it doesn’t show anything, and I understand how that sounds, but I know it ties back to them somehow. I just want someone to listen and maybe help me explain it the right way.
When people show you records that seem to contradict your concern, are you still certain your husband’s family is behind it?

I mean… I don’t want to sound unreasonable, and I know records are supposed to be facts. But yes, I still feel pretty sure it’s them. Maybe not in a way that shows up neatly on paper, but these little billing problems and the way people act toward me… it keeps happening, and it all points back to my husband’s family somehow. Does that make sense?
Have you had the feeling that anyone can put thoughts into your mind or control your thoughts?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have a lot on my mind, obviously, but it feels like my own thoughts. I haven’t felt like someone was putting them there or controlling them… if that’s what you mean.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I might think I hear something and then realize it’s the TV or someone outside, but not voices talking to me when no one’s there. That’s not really what’s been happening.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, energetic, or euphoric for several days in a row?

Um… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I have days where I get a little wound up or I’m trying to get a lot done, but not like unusually high or euphoric for days. At least not that I’ve noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
For at least two weeks at a time, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t think it’s been like that, no. I mean, I have bad days and I get discouraged, but depressed most of the day nearly every day for two weeks… I don’t think so. At least, I wouldn’t describe it that way.
Have you had any major medical or neurological illness that started before or around the time these concerns began?

Not that I know of, no. I mean, I haven’t had anything major like that start around then. I’m not sure exactly what would count, but nothing a doctor told me was a serious medical or neurological illness. Does that answer it okay?
Do you believe your husband’s family has abilities that are impossible in ordinary life, like secretly reading your thoughts or influencing events in ways normal people couldn’t?

I wouldn’t say it like they’re reading my thoughts or something impossible, no. It’s more… they have ways of getting to people, quietly. Like with our money, or making things look bad for me—little billing errors at work, or someone at church suddenly acting strange toward me. I know it sounds like I’m making too much of it, and I’m not trying to sound unreasonable, but it keeps tying back to his family no matter what records people show me. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling sure that your husband’s family is interfering with your money or reputation?

I guess it’s been… about nine months now. It started after that trouble with his family about money and the holiday expectations. I didn’t want to make it sound like I’ve been obsessing over it or anything, but that’s when I really started feeling sure something was going on. Is that the kind of time frame you mean?
Because of this situation, has your ability to work or manage your usual daily responsibilities clearly gotten worse?

No, I wouldn’t say it’s clearly gotten worse. I mean, I still get up and go to work, and I do my billing clerk duties. At home I keep things going, and I still garden or paint when I can.

The main problem is more when I try to warn people about what my in-laws are doing. That’s when it can get awkward or people act like I’m making trouble. But day to day, I’m functioning okay, I think. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Before this started nine months ago, did you generally tend to mistrust other people or suspect they meant to harm or deceive you?

I don’t think so… not in any big way. I mean, I’ve always tried to be careful with people, like anyone would, but I wouldn’t say I went around thinking people were out to get me before all this.

Maybe I worried sometimes, but not like this. Is that what you mean?
Have other people told you that your speech or the way you explain things has become hard to follow or jumbled?

No, I don’t think anyone has said that exactly. I mean, maybe people don’t always agree with what I’m saying, or they get impatient, but I haven’t been told my speech is jumbled or hard to follow.

I try to explain things clearly. If I’m not answering that the right way, you can tell me.
Aside from your concerns about your husband’s family, have you had any other unusual experiences that felt clearly real to you but that other people said weren’t happening?

Not really other kinds of things, no… I mean, it’s mostly this situation with my husband’s family.

I know it may sound like I’m connecting things, but when little billing errors show up at work, or someone at church suddenly acts strange toward me, it just fits with what they’ve been doing to our money and our reputation. Even when people show me records or say there’s no proof, I still know it traces back to them somehow.

I’m not trying to sound unreasonable. That’s just what keeps happening from my side of it.
Have you felt that outside forces were controlling your actions or movements?

No… I don’t think so. I’ve never felt like something outside of me was moving my body or making me do things like that.

I mean, I can get stressed and feel pressured by what’s going on, but my actions feel like mine. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Over the past several months, have you become much less interested in seeing people or doing things you used to enjoy?

No, not much less, I don’t think. I mean, I still get up and go to work, and I handle my billing duties. I keep the house going, too.

I still like my gardening, and I paint when I can. So I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped enjoying things. The main difficulty is more when I try to warn people about what my in-laws are doing, and then people get uncomfortable or don’t want to hear it. But I’m still doing my regular things, if that makes sense.
Did this belief about your husband’s family begin very suddenly, over a day or two?

No, not over just a day or two. It’s been more gradual than that… or, well, it really started around the trouble with his family over money and the holiday expectations.

That was about nine months ago, I think. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but since then it’s just been ongoing. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you felt that other people could know your thoughts even when you had not said them out loud?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t felt like people can actually hear or know my thoughts if I don’t say them.

Sometimes I might feel like people are reading too much into me, or judging my expression maybe, but not like they can know what I’m thinking. Is that what you mean?
